commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: artifact-diagramming
commands.description: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts - when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.

commands.name: artifact-capabilities
commands.description: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, or handing the viewer a file to save. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever any such runtime behavior would make an artifact more useful, before writing the page.

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug
commands.description: Enable debug logging for this session and help diagnose issues

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.

commands.name: simplify
commands.description: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

commands.name: batch
commands.description: Research and plan a large-scale change, then execute it in parallel across 5–30 isolated worktree agents that each open a PR.

commands.name: fewer-permission-prompts
commands.description: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.

commands.name: doctor
commands.description: Health-check the user's Claude Code setup and fix issues: diagnose installation health — what the `claude doctor` terminal diagnostics cover — from local data (duplicate or leftover installs, PATH, unparseable settings files, broken or colliding agent definitions, skills whose frontmatter fails to parse); find unused skills, MCP servers, and plugins versus their context cost and disable dead weight; deduplicate local CLAUDE.md files against checked-in ones; trim checked-in CLAUDE.md files by cutting content a session could derive from the codebase (directory layouts, tech-stack lists, architecture overviews) while keeping gotchas, rationale, and non-standard conventions; migrate always-loaded CLAUDE.md guidance into lazy skills and nested CLAUDE.md files; flag slow hooks and context-heavy extensions; check the installed version is current; make auto mode the default permission mode; and pre-approve frequently denied read-only commands. Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

commands.name: loop
commands.description: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace.

commands.name: claude-api
commands.description:
Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).

commands.name: docs
commands.description: docs (editable docs people share and comment on; the default for any document, named as a doc or not: a document, report, proposal, resume, cover letter, letter, contract, policy, form, template, worksheet, essay, handbook, guide, how-to, cheat sheet, SOP or other writing to keep, share, collaborate on, send, submit, print or sign; a doc exports to Word, PDF, Markdown or Google Docs, so needing a file to send, attach, upload, submit or print is no reason to pick Word, and a file nobody asked for is a doc, not Word; a plan, comparison, summary or notes asked in chat stays in chat; a pasted claude.ai artifact link may be a doc: check with docs tools first; Word or another file format named, tracked changes wanted, or a .docx to change or use as a template → that format's skill): making one → if no docs-connector instructions are in context, call its `guide` (topic.instructions) first; then create the doc (headings only, no body) before any search, file read or plan, even with files attached. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: docx
commands.description: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx) or Word templates (.dotx). Triggers include: any mention of Microsoft Word Documents, such as 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', 'microsoft doc'. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a deliverable as a Word or .docx file (to download, email or print), use this skill. However, if they ask for a document, page, report, memo, or notes WITHOUT naming a file format and the session offers Claude's own dedicated document or page skill or connector, use that instead, even if they will email or print it. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or coding unrelated to document generation. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: google-workspace
commands.description: Read this before the first Google Drive, Docs, Sheets or Slides connector call whenever the task creates or changes a Google file. Use this skill whenever the user wants to create or change a Google Doc, Sheet or Slides file in their Google Drive. Triggers include: a request that names Google Docs, Sheets, Slides or Drive and asks to make, edit, format, copy or rename a file; a docs.google.com link with a request to change that file, even a one-line fix or suggested edits; and any follow-up change to a Google file from earlier in the chat, even "change it" or "add a tab". Includes helper scripts for document positions, cell ranges and slide layout. However, if the user asks for a doc, deck or spreadsheet without naming Google, or gives a Google file only as source material for something new, use Claude's own output type instead. Do NOT use for read-only questions about a Google file, or for Word, Excel, PowerPoint or PDF files. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: import-memory
commands.description: Import a memory export from another AI assistant into Claude's memory — conversationally, additively, and with the content treated as data. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: morning
commands.description: Render the user's morning brief as a styled HTML artifact, or set it up as a recurring weekday task. Use only when the user explicitly asks to run, see, or set up their morning brief, or if they invoke /morning by name. A question about their day, schedule, or calendar is not by itself a request for the brief; answer it directly instead. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: pdf
commands.description: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: pptx
commands.description: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations as PowerPoint (.pptx) files; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email, summary, or creating a different type of slide deck); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user asks for a PowerPoint or .pptx file, or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. However, when the user asks for a deck, slides, a slide deck, or a presentation without naming a file format, default to using a dedicated slide-deck artifact type or a separate slides skill if this session offers one; otherwise, use this skill. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: skill-creator
commands.description: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: xlsx
commands.description: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved. (claude.ai sync)

34	
35	| P3 finding | RC2 disposition |
36	|---|---|
37	| F1 Q10 unestablished | **Production evidence (founder-run, read-only, 2026-10-01, `pg_stat_user_tables`):** `member_manuscripts` 21 rows / 48 kB · `living_works` 8 / 48 kB · `proposal_chains` 9 / 96 kB. Row counts are statistics estimates; on-disk sizes confirm the scale. Lock *hold* time for the constraint/index builds is negligible at this size. Concurrent index builds are deliberately not used. |
38	| F2 lock acquisition | Each of the three migrations sets `SET LOCAL lock_timeout = '5s'` inside its own transaction. A timeout aborts that file before the reader swap, with the old reader intact. |

The target routes and `contract.ts` are added to the minimum Reads below (Q8). |

42	| Duplicate precheck (founder) | Migration 1's `UNIQUE (id, member_id)` cannot meet duplicates, because `id` is already each table's primary key. Pre-deploy read-only witness, expected to return zero rows: `SELECT id, member_id, count(*) FROM living_works GROUP BY 1,2 HAVING count(*) > 1;` (and the same for `member_manuscripts`). Any row is a founder dedupe decision, never a migration action. |

44	Disposable PostgreSQL 16 witness of the RC2 bytes (stub prerequisite schema), from a fresh database each time:
45	fresh apply 1→2→3 PASS · re-run 1, 2, 3 after commit PASS · migration 2 with one pre-successor episode refuses and leaves prefix 1 (no `locus_scope_kind`, `requested_scope` intact) · migration 1 behind a held `ACCESS SHARE` transaction fails after 5 s with `lock timeout` and changes nothing.

1	#!/bin/bash
2	# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
3	# MAIA Sovereign - Production Deployment Script
4	# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
5	# Usage:
6	#   ./scripts/deploy-production.sh [command]
7	#
8	# Commands:
9	#   setup     - First-time setup (generate secrets, prepare env)
10	#   deploy    - Build and deploy the full stack
11	#   update    - Pull latest code and redeploy
12	#   rollback  - Rollback to previous deployment (2-command rollback)
13	#   safe-mode - Toggle safe mode (on/off) for degraded operation
14	#   migrate   - Run database migrations
15	#   logs      - Tail container logs
16	#   status    - Show container status
17	#   stop      - Stop all containers
18	#   backup    - Backup database to file
19	#   restore   - Restore database from backup
20	#
21	# Stability Features:
22	#   - Image tagging by git SHA for instant rollbacks
23	#   - Safe mode toggle for degraded operation
24	#   - Smoke tests with automatic alerts
25	# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
26	
27	set -e
28	
29	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
30	PROJECT_DIR="$(dirname "$SCRIPT_DIR")"
31	COMPOSE_FILE="$PROJECT_DIR/docker-compose.production.yml"
32	
33	# Deploy lane lock — every mutating command serializes on $PROJECT_DIR/.deploy.lock
34	# so concurrent deploys are structurally impossible (see scripts/deploy-lock.sh).
35	source "$SCRIPT_DIR/deploy-lock.sh"
36	
37	# Rollback tagging — shared with pre-deploy-gate.sh so EVERY deploy path keeps
38	# maia-sovereign:current/:previous/:<sha> truthful (see scripts/deploy-tag.sh).
39	source "$SCRIPT_DIR/deploy-tag.sh"
40	
41	# Immutable-SHA build context — deploy/update build a NAMED commit materialized
42	# into an isolated context, never whatever branch is checked out in the shared
43	# repo (2026-07-27 incident). See scripts/deploy-context.sh + docs/ops/IMMUTABLE_SHA_DEPLOY.md.
44	source "$SCRIPT_DIR/deploy-context.sh"
45	
46	# Colors for output
47	RED='\033[0;31m'
48	GREEN='\033[0;32m'
49	YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
50	BLUE='\033[0;34m'
51	NC='\033[0m' # No Color
52	
53	log_info() { echo -e "${BLUE}[INFO]${NC} $1"; }
54	log_success() { echo -e "${GREEN}[OK]${NC} $1"; }
55	log_warn() { echo -e "${YELLOW}[WARN]${NC} $1"; }

59	run_dependency_security_audit() {
60	    local manifest="${MAIA_BUILD_CONTEXT:-$PROJECT_DIR}/package.json"
61	    local declared manager fix_hint
62	    local -a audit_cmd
63	
64	    declared="$(node -p "require('$manifest').packageManager || ''" 2>/dev/null || true)"
65	    manager="${declared%%@*}"
66	    if [ -z "$manager" ]; then
67	        if [ -f "${MAIA_BUILD_CONTEXT:-$PROJECT_DIR}/package-lock.json" ]; then
68	            manager="npm"
69	        elif [ -f "${MAIA_BUILD_CONTEXT:-$PROJECT_DIR}/pnpm-lock.yaml" ]; then
70	            manager="pnpm"
71	        fi
72	    fi
73	
74	    log_info "Running dependency security audit${declared:+ (declared $declared)}..."
75	
76	    case "$manager" in
77	        npm)
78	            command -v npm >/dev/null 2>&1 || { log_error "Declared package manager npm is unavailable — dependency audit cannot run."; return 1; }
79	            audit_cmd=(npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=moderate)
80	            fix_hint="npm audit fix"
81	            ;;
82	        pnpm)
83	            command -v pnpm >/dev/null 2>&1 || { log_error "Declared package manager pnpm is unavailable — dependency audit cannot run."; return 1; }
84	            audit_cmd=(pnpm audit --prod --audit-level=moderate)
85	            fix_hint="pnpm audit --fix"
86	            ;;
87	        *)
88	            log_error "No supported package manager could be resolved from the target snapshot."
89	            return 1
90	            ;;
91	    esac

93	    if ! "${audit_cmd[@]}" 2>&1; then
94	        log_error "Dependency audit failed — moderate+ production vulnerabilities detected."
95	        log_error "Review and remediate deliberately; do not apply fixes blindly."

102	
103	# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
104	# MIGRATIONS - fail closed
105	# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
106	# DEPLOYMENT-SAFETY-01 (founder ruling 2026-09-14). The migration runner already
107	# exits non-zero on the first failing file; both deploy paths used to catch that
108	# with `if ! …; then log_warn …; fi` and carry on to "Deployment complete!".
109	#
110	# That swallow broke the migrations README's own rule — *schema and reader ship
111	# together* — IN THE FAILURE DIRECTION: the schema could fail while the reader
112	# continued toward production, and the operator was told the deploy succeeded.
113	# A green deploy was not evidence that any migration ran.
114	#
115	#   migration success  →  deployment may continue
116	#   migration failure  →  deployment STOPS, non-zero, no success message
117	#
118	# DEPLOYMENT-SAFETY-03 / STEP 3 strengthens the ordering after the original
119	# fail-closed repair: an exact admitted review must establish final-schema and
120	# every-prefix old-reader compatibility before pending migrations may run.
121	#
122	# Normal deploy/update now order:
123	#   build → image provenance → review/compatibility gate
124	#         → re-witness pending set + old reader → migrate
125	#         → rollback tags → candidate swap → running provenance
126	#
127	# A migration failure therefore leaves the candidate reader unswapped. Because
128	# the runner commits each migration independently, the admitted review must also
129	# cover every successfully committed prefix that could remain after failure.
130	#
131	# ⛔ NOT CHANGED: migration discovery, selection, per-file transaction semantics,
132	# the ledger, migration contents, or the migration-only command's role.
133	# REVIEW-CUSTODY-01 / STEP 3 — production migration review preflight.
134	#
135	# This belongs at the DEPLOYMENT surface, not in the generic local migration
136	# engine. Bootstrap/test/reconstruction databases are not production authority.
137	# The pending set is derived read-only from the exact migration context + ledger,
138	# and every pending SQL file must carry a physically witnessed Read event.
139	_review_migration_compose() {
140	    if [ -n "${MAIA_BUILD_CONTEXT:-}" ]; then
141	        deploy_ctx_compose "$@"
142	    else
143	        docker compose -f "$COMPOSE_FILE" "$@"
144	    fi
145	}
146	
147	collect_pending_production_migrations() {
148	    local raw
149	    if ! raw="$(_review_migration_compose --profile migrate run --rm -T migrate sh -c '
150	        set -eu
151	        ledger="$(mktemp)"
152	        trap '"'"'rm -f "$ledger"'"'"' EXIT
153	        psql "$DATABASE_URL" -Atc "SELECT filename FROM schema_migrations WHERE filename IS NOT NULL ORDER BY 1" > "$ledger"
154	        for f in /app/database/migrations/*.sql; do
155	            [ -e "$f" ] || continue
156	            b="${f##*/}"
157	            if ! grep -Fxq "$b" "$ledger"; then
158	                printf "database/migrations/%s\n" "$b"
159	            fi
160	        done
161	    ')"; then
162	        log_error "⛔ Could not derive the production-pending migration set read-only."
163	        log_error "   REVIEW-CUSTODY refuses rather than guessing what would execute."
164	        return 1
165	    fi
166	    printf '%s\n' "$raw" | grep -E '^database/migrations/[^/]+\.sql$' || true
167	}
168	
169	review_migration_custody_or_abort() {
170	    local phase="$1"
171	
172	    # Cache only observations that have actually passed the composed gate.
173	    # Step 3 will re-witness them immediately before schema mutation.
174	    MIGRATION_COMPAT_EXPECTED_PENDING=""
175	    MIGRATION_COMPAT_EXPECTED_OLD_READER=""
176	
177	    local target="${DEPLOY_CTX_FULL_SHA:-}"
178	    if [ -z "$target" ]; then
179	        target="$(git -C "$PROJECT_DIR" rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null || true)"
180	    fi
181	    if [ -z "$target" ]; then
182	        log_error "⛔ REVIEW-CUSTODY cannot resolve the exact migration target commit."
183	        return 1
184	    fi
185	
186	    local pending
187	    if ! pending="$(collect_pending_production_migrations)"; then
188	        log_error "$phase aborted before migration: pending-set witness failed."
189	        return 1
190	    fi
191	    MIGRATION_COMPAT_EXPECTED_PENDING="$pending"
192	    if [ -z "$pending" ]; then
193	        log_info "REVIEW-CUSTODY: no production-pending migrations; no migration review required."
194	        return 0
195	    fi
196	
197	    local record="${REVIEW_CUSTODY_RECORD:-}"
198	    local review="${REVIEW_CUSTODY_REVIEW:-}"
199	    local trace="${REVIEW_CUSTODY_TRACE:-}"
200	    if [ -z "$record" ] || [ -z "$review" ] || [ -z "$trace" ]; then
201	        log_error "════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════"
202	        log_error "⛔ DATABASE MIGRATION REVIEW REQUIRED — $phase REFUSED"
203	        log_error "════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════"
204	        log_error "Pending migrations exist, but the bound evidence triplet is incomplete."
205	        log_error "Set REVIEW_CUSTODY_RECORD, REVIEW_CUSTODY_REVIEW, REVIEW_CUSTODY_TRACE."
206	        log_error "Self-reported coverage is not accepted."
207	        printf '%s\n' "$pending" | sed 's/^/  pending: /' >&2
208	        return 1
209	    fi
210	
211	    local gate_root="${MAIA_BUILD_CONTEXT:-$PROJECT_DIR}"
212	    local gate="$gate_root/scripts/review-custody-migration-gate.ts"
213	    if [ ! -f "$gate" ]; then
214	        log_error "⛔ Migration review gate is absent from target context: $gate"
215	        return 1
216	    fi
217	    local tsx_bin="$PROJECT_DIR/node_modules/.bin/tsx"
218	    if [ ! -x "$tsx_bin" ]; then
219	        log_error "⛔ Migration review gate cannot execute: host tsx unavailable at $tsx_bin"
220	        return 1
221	    fi
222	
223	    # DEPLOYMENT-SAFETY-03 / STEP 2B: compatibility is relational to
224	    # the reader that is actually live before any swap. Missing/unresolvable
225	    # identity refuses; a guessed old reader would make compatibility meaningless.
226	    local old_stamp old_reader
227	    old_stamp="$(docker exec maia-sovereign printenv GIT_COMMIT 2>/dev/null || true)"
228	    if [ -z "$old_stamp" ]; then
229	        log_error "⛔ MIGRATION-COMPATIBILITY cannot identify the currently running reader."
230	        return 1
231	    fi
232	    old_reader="$(git -C "$PROJECT_DIR" rev-parse "$old_stamp^{commit}" 2>/dev/null || true)"
233	    if [ -z "$old_reader" ]; then
234	        log_error "⛔ Running reader stamp does not resolve to a repository commit: $old_stamp"
235	        return 1
236	    fi
237	
238	    local args=(--record "$record" --review "$review" --trace "$trace"
239	                --repo "$PROJECT_DIR" --target "$target" --old-reader "$old_reader")
240	    local m
241	    while IFS= read -r m; do
242	        [ -n "$m" ] && args+=(--migration "$m")
243	    done <<< "$pending"
244	
245	    log_info "REVIEW-CUSTODY + MIGRATION-COMPATIBILITY: checking exact pending relation..."
246	    if ! "$tsx_bin" "$gate" "${args[@]}"; then
247	        log_error "⛔ $phase aborted before migration: review/compatibility gate does not apply."
248	        return 1
249	    fi
250	    MIGRATION_COMPAT_EXPECTED_OLD_READER="$old_reader"
251	    log_success "Migration review custody + old-reader compatibility apply to the exact pending set"
252	}
253	
254	rewitness_migration_relation_or_abort() {
255	    local phase="$1"
256	    local expected_pending="${MIGRATION_COMPAT_EXPECTED_PENDING-}"
257	    local expected_old="${MIGRATION_COMPAT_EXPECTED_OLD_READER-}"
258	
259	    # Re-derive the mutable ledger relation immediately before mutation. The
260	    # target tree is immutable; the production ledger and live reader are not.
261	    local pending_now
262	    if ! pending_now="$(collect_pending_production_migrations)"; then
263	        log_error "⛔ $phase aborted before migration: could not re-witness the pending set."
264	        return 1
265	    fi
266	    if [ "$pending_now" != "$expected_pending" ]; then
267	        log_error "⛔ $phase aborted before migration: pending migration state moved after review."
268	        log_error "   The compatibility claim applies only to the exact ordered set it reviewed."
269	        return 1
270	    fi
271	
272	    # If there is schema work to do, the old reader is the load-bearing recovery
273	    # relation. Read it LAST, immediately before the migration runner.
274	    if [ -n "$expected_pending" ]; then
275	        if [ -z "$expected_old" ]; then
276	            log_error "⛔ $phase aborted before migration: no reviewed old-reader identity is cached."
277	            return 1
278	        fi
279	
280	        local live_stamp live_old
281	        live_stamp="$(docker exec maia-sovereign printenv GIT_COMMIT 2>/dev/null || true)"
282	        if [ -z "$live_stamp" ]; then
283	            log_error "⛔ $phase aborted before migration: the live reader identity cannot be read."
284	            return 1
285	        fi
286	        live_old="$(git -C "$PROJECT_DIR" rev-parse "$live_stamp^{commit}" 2>/dev/null || true)"
287	        if [ -z "$live_old" ] || [ "$live_old" != "$expected_old" ]; then
288	            log_error "⛔ $phase aborted before migration: the live reader moved after compatibility review."
289	            log_error "   reviewed: $expected_old"
290	            log_error "   live:     ${live_old:-unresolved}"
291	            return 1
292	        fi
293	        log_success "Old reader re-witnessed immediately before migration: $live_old"
294	    fi
295	}

297	run_migrations_or_abort() {
298	    local phase="$1"
299	
300	    # STEP 3 ordering law: no schema mutation occurs unless the mutable parts of
301	    # the reviewed relation still match at the last possible pre-migration point.
302	    if ! rewitness_migration_relation_or_abort "$phase"; then
303	        exit 1
304	    fi
305	
306	    log_info "Running database migrations before candidate swap..."
307	    if deploy_ctx_compose --profile migrate run --rm migrate; then
308	        log_success "Migrations applied before candidate swap"
309	        return 0
310	    fi
311	
312	    echo ""
313	    log_error "════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════"
314	    log_error "⛔ DATABASE MIGRATIONS FAILED — DEPLOYMENT ABORTED PRE-SWAP"
315	    log_error "════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════"
316	    log_error ""
317	    log_error "The candidate reader was NOT swapped in."
318	    log_error "The previously witnessed old reader remains the live reader."
319	    log_error "Any earlier migration in this run that committed successfully was"
320	    log_error "required by the admitted review to leave that old reader compatible"
321	    log_error "at every committed prefix."
322	    log_error ""
323	    log_error "The runner stops at the first failing file. Later migrations are"
324	    log_error "unapplied and this deployment is NOT complete."
325	    log_error ""
326	    log_error "Inspect what committed and what remains before any retry:"
327	    log_error "  docker exec maia-postgres psql -U soullab -d maia_consciousness \\"
328	    log_error "    -c \"SELECT filename FROM schema_migrations ORDER BY applied_at DESC LIMIT 10;\""
329	    log_error ""
330	    log_error "Do not swap the candidate reader until a newly applicable review/"
331	    log_error "compatibility record governs the remaining exact pending set."
332	    log_error "════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════"
333	    echo ""
334	    log_error "$phase aborted pre-swap: migrations did not succeed."

339	# ALERT - Send alert to developer via /api/build/alert
340	# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
341	send_alert() {
342	    local severity="$1"
343	    local message="$2"
344	    local details="${3:-}"
345	
346	    # Get BASE_URL from env file (quote-safe, whitespace-trimmed), allow env override
347	    local base_url
348	    base_url=$(awk -F= '/^BASE_URL=/{gsub(/^"|"$/,"",$2); gsub(/^[ \t]+|[ \t]+$/,"",$2); print $2}' .env.production 2>/dev/null | tail -n 1)
349	    base_url="${BASE_URL:-${base_url:-https://soullab.life}}"
350	    base_url="${base_url%/}"  # Strip trailing slash
351	
352	    # Get alert token from env file (quote-safe, whitespace-trimmed), allow env override
353	    local alert_token
354	    alert_token=$(awk -F= '/^INTERNAL_ALERT_TOKEN=/{gsub(/^"|"$/,"",$2); gsub(/^[ \t]+|[ \t]+$/,"",$2); print $2}' .env.production 2>/dev/null | tail -n 1)
355	    alert_token="${INTERNAL_ALERT_TOKEN:-$alert_token}"
356	
357	    # Build JSON payload safely using jq if available
358	    local json_payload
359	    if command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
360	        if [ -n "$details" ]; then
361	            # Validate details is valid JSON, otherwise treat as string
362	            if echo "$details" | jq -e . >/dev/null 2>&1; then
363	                json_payload=$(jq -n \
364	                    --arg sev "$severity" \
365	                    --arg msg "$message" \
366	                    --arg commit "${GIT_COMMIT:-unknown}" \
367	                    --argjson details "$details" \
368	                    '{severity:$sev, message:$msg, commit:$commit, source:"deploy-script", details:$details}')
369	            else
370	                json_payload=$(jq -n \
371	                    --arg sev "$severity" \
372	                    --arg msg "$message" \
373	                    --arg commit "${GIT_COMMIT:-unknown}" \
374	                    --arg details "$details" \
375	                    '{severity:$sev, message:$msg, commit:$commit, source:"deploy-script", details:$details}')
376	            fi
377	        else
378	            json_payload=$(jq -n \
379	                --arg sev "$severity" \
380	                --arg msg "$message" \
381	                --arg commit "${GIT_COMMIT:-unknown}" \
382	                '{severity:$sev, message:$msg, commit:$commit, source:"deploy-script"}')
383	        fi
384	    else
385	        # Fallback: escape quotes in message
386	        local escaped_msg
387	        escaped_msg=$(echo "$message" | sed 's/\\/\\\\/g; s/"/\\"/g')
388	        if [ -n "$details" ]; then
389	            json_payload="{\"severity\": \"$severity\", \"message\": \"$escaped_msg\", \"commit\": \"${GIT_COMMIT:-unknown}\", \"source\": \"deploy-script\", \"details\": $details}"
390	        else
391	            json_payload="{\"severity\": \"$severity\", \"message\": \"$escaped_msg\", \"commit\": \"${GIT_COMMIT:-unknown}\", \"source\": \"deploy-script\"}"
392	        fi
393	    fi
394	
395	    curl -sf -X POST "${base_url}/api/build/alert" \
396	        -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
397	        -H "x-internal-token: ${alert_token}" \
398	        -d "$json_payload" > /dev/null 2>&1 || log_warn "Alert send failed (non-critical)"
399	}

402	# SMOKE TESTS - Run post-deployment health checks
403	# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
404	run_smoke_tests() {
405	    log_info "Running post-deployment smoke tests..."
406	
407	    # Quote-safe, whitespace-trimmed BASE_URL parsing, allow env override
408	    local base_url
409	    base_url=$(awk -F= '/^BASE_URL=/{gsub(/^"|"$/,"",$2); gsub(/^[ \t]+|[ \t]+$/,"",$2); print $2}' .env.production 2>/dev/null | tail -n 1)
410	    base_url="${BASE_URL:-${base_url:-https://soullab.life}}"
411	    base_url="${base_url%/}"  # Strip trailing slash
412	
413	    log_info "  Target: $base_url"
414	
415	    local all_passed=true
416	    local report=""
417	    add_result() { report="${report}\n  $1"; }
418	
419	    # Wait for Next.js cold start (standalone server needs time)
420	    log_info "  Waiting for services to stabilize..."
421	    sleep 8
422	
423	    # Helper: retry a curl check up to N times with backoff (explicit timeouts)
424	    retry_curl() {
425	        local url="$1"
426	        local max_attempts="${2:-3}"
427	        local attempt=1
428	        while [ $attempt -le $max_attempts ]; do
429	            if curl -sf --connect-timeout 3 --max-time 8 "$url" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
430	                return 0
431	            fi
432	            sleep 2
433	            attempt=$((attempt + 1))
434	        done
435	        return 1
436	    }
437	
438	    # Test 1: Health endpoint (with retry for cold start)
439	    log_info "  Testing /api/health..."
440	    if retry_curl "${base_url}/api/health" 3; then
441	        log_success "  /api/health OK"
442	        add_result "PASS  /api/health"
443	    else
444	        log_error "  /api/health FAILED"
445	        add_result "FAIL  /api/health (unreachable after retries)"
446	        send_alert "critical" "Health endpoint failed after deployment"
447	        all_passed=false
448	    fi
449	
450	    # Test 2: Version endpoint (with retry for cold start)
451	    log_info "  Testing /api/version..."
452	    if retry_curl "${base_url}/api/version" 3; then
453	        log_success "  /api/version OK"
454	        add_result "PASS  /api/version"
455	    else
456	        log_error "  /api/version FAILED"
457	        add_result "FAIL  /api/version (unreachable after retries)"
458	        send_alert "critical" "Version endpoint failed after deployment"
459	        all_passed=false
460	    fi
461	
462	    # Test 3: Ready endpoint (checks dependencies)
463	    log_info "  Testing /api/ready..."
464	    local ready_response
465	    ready_response=$(curl -sf --connect-timeout 3 --max-time 8 "${base_url}/api/ready" 2>/dev/null || echo '{"ready":false}')
466	    if echo "$ready_response" | grep -q '"ready":true'; then
467	        log_success "  /api/ready OK"
468	        add_result "PASS  /api/ready"
469	    else
470	        log_warn "  /api/ready shows degraded dependencies"
471	        add_result "WARN  /api/ready (degraded dependencies)"
472	        # Build safe JSON payload for alert
473	        local ready_snip
474	        ready_snip="$(echo "$ready_response" | head -c 500)"
475	        local payload
476	        if command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
477	            payload="$(jq -n --arg response "$ready_snip" '{response:$response}')"
478	        else
479	            payload="{\"response\":\"$(echo "$ready_snip" | sed 's/\\/\\\\/g; s/"/\\"/g')\"}"
480	        fi
481	        send_alert "warning" "Dependencies degraded after deployment" "$payload"
482	    fi
483	
484	    # Test 4: Main page loads
485	    log_info "  Testing main page..."
486	    if curl -sf --connect-timeout 3 --max-time 10 "${base_url}/" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
487	        log_success "  Main page OK"
488	        add_result "PASS  Main page"
489	    else
490	        log_warn "  Main page may be slow to respond"
491	        add_result "WARN  Main page (slow or unreachable)"
492	    fi
493	
494	    # Test 5: Auth endpoints are locked (with retry for cold start)
495	    # Helper for status code checks with retry
496	    get_status_code_with_retry() {
497	        local url="$1"
498	        local method="${2:-GET}"
499	        local max_attempts=3
500	        local attempt=1
501	        local code
502	        while [ $attempt -le $max_attempts ]; do
503	            if [ "$method" = "POST" ]; then
504	                code=$(curl -sS --connect-timeout 3 --max-time 8 -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -X POST "$url" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{}' 2>/dev/null)
505	            else
506	                code=$(curl -sS --connect-timeout 3 --max-time 8 -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" "$url" 2>/dev/null)
507	            fi
508	            # If we got a real response (not warmup noise), return it
509	            # 000 = curl couldn't connect, 500/502/504 = gateway errors during boot
510	            if [ "$code" != "000" ] && [ "$code" != "500" ] && [ "$code" != "502" ] && [ "$code" != "504" ]; then
511	                echo "$code"
512	                return 0
513	            fi
514	            sleep 2
515	            attempt=$((attempt + 1))
516	        done
517	        echo "$code"  # Return last code even if it's 500
518	    }
519	
520	    # Only accept HTTP→HTTPS redirects when testing localhost (prevents masking real security issues)
521	    local allow_redirect_as_pass=false
522	    if echo "$base_url" | grep -qE '^http://(localhost|127\.0\.0\.1)(:|/|$)'; then
523	        allow_redirect_as_pass=true
524	    fi
525	
526	    log_info "  Testing auth lock on /api/build/status..."
527	    local status_code
528	    status_code=$(get_status_code_with_retry "${base_url}/api/build/status" "GET")
529	    if [ "$status_code" = "000" ]; then
530	        log_error "  /api/build/status unreachable (000) — check routing/DNS/caddy"
531	        add_result "FAIL  /api/build/status (000 - routing issue)"
532	        all_passed=false
533	    elif $allow_redirect_as_pass && { [ "$status_code" = "301" ] || [ "$status_code" = "308" ]; }; then
534	        # HTTP→HTTPS redirect is acceptable for localhost smoke tests only
535	        log_success "  /api/build/status redirects to HTTPS ($status_code) — acceptable for localhost HTTP smoke only"
536	        add_result "PASS  /api/build/status (redirect: $status_code, localhost only)"
537	    elif [ "$status_code" = "401" ] || [ "$status_code" = "403" ] || [ "$status_code" = "503" ]; then
538	        log_success "  /api/build/status locked ($status_code)"
539	        add_result "PASS  /api/build/status (locked: $status_code)"
540	    else
541	        log_error "  /api/build/status NOT LOCKED (got $status_code, expected 401/403/503)"
542	        add_result "FAIL  /api/build/status (got $status_code, not locked)"
543	        send_alert "critical" "Build status endpoint is not protected!" "{\"http_code\": \"$status_code\"}"
544	        all_passed=false
545	    fi
546	
547	    log_info "  Testing auth lock on /api/build/alert..."
548	    status_code=$(get_status_code_with_retry "${base_url}/api/build/alert" "POST")
549	    if [ "$status_code" = "000" ]; then
550	        log_error "  /api/build/alert unreachable (000) — check routing/DNS/caddy"
551	        add_result "FAIL  /api/build/alert (000 - routing issue)"
552	        all_passed=false
553	    elif $allow_redirect_as_pass && { [ "$status_code" = "301" ] || [ "$status_code" = "308" ]; }; then
554	        # HTTP→HTTPS redirect is acceptable for localhost smoke tests only
555	        log_success "  /api/build/alert redirects to HTTPS ($status_code) — acceptable for localhost HTTP smoke only"
556	        add_result "PASS  /api/build/alert (redirect: $status_code, localhost only)"
557	    elif [ "$status_code" = "401" ] || [ "$status_code" = "403" ] || [ "$status_code" = "503" ]; then
558	        log_success "  /api/build/alert locked ($status_code)"
559	        add_result "PASS  /api/build/alert (locked: $status_code)"
560	    else
561	        log_error "  /api/build/alert NOT LOCKED (got $status_code, expected 401/403/503)"
562	        add_result "FAIL  /api/build/alert (got $status_code, not locked)"
563	        send_alert "critical" "Build alert endpoint is not protected!" "{\"http_code\": \"$status_code\"}"
564	        all_passed=false
565	    fi
566	
567	    # ── Constitutional Verification Gate ───────────────────────────────────────
568	    # Runs the full constitutional verification suite inside the container.
569	    # Checks all five subsystems: Co-Lab, Memory, Relationships, Development, MAIA.
570	    # Skipped gracefully if the orchestrator is absent (first-time deploys).
571	    # A non-zero exit is a hard release failure.
572	    #
573	    # Gate invariant: a release is not ready because the UI looks correct —
574	    # it is ready when the platform proves it still honors its constitution.
575	    log_info "  Running constitutional verification..."
576	    if docker exec maia-sovereign test -f /app/scripts/constitutional-verification.sh 2>/dev/null; then
577	        local cv_output

580	            log_success "  Constitutional verification: PASSED"

664	# DEPLOY - Build and start the stack
665	# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
666	cmd_deploy() {
667	    local ref="${1:-}"
668	    # The lock record names the ASSERTED target (the SHA on the command line),
669	    # never the shared checkout's HEAD — see scripts/deploy-lock.sh.
670	    acquire_deploy_lock "deploy-production.sh deploy" "$ref"
671	    log_info "Deploying MAIA Sovereign..."
672	
673	    cd "$PROJECT_DIR"
674	
675	    # Name a commit and snapshot it into an isolated build context BEFORE any
676	    # build work. Refuses when no SHA is named (unless DEPLOY_ALLOW_HEAD=1). This
677	    # is the structural guarantee that the full deploy builds an explicitly named
678	    # immutable commit, never whichever branch happens to be checked out in the
679	    # shared repo. Sets MAIA_BUILD_CONTEXT + GIT_COMMIT.
680	    deploy_ctx_assert_and_materialize "$ref" || exit 1
681	
682	    # Verify .env.production exists
683	    if [ ! -f ".env.production" ]; then
684	        log_error ".env.production not found. Run: ./scripts/deploy-production.sh setup"
685	        exit 1
686	    fi
687	
688	    # Check required values are set
689	    if grep -q "REPLACE_ME" .env.production; then
690	        log_error "Please replace all REPLACE_ME values in .env.production"
691	        exit 1
692	    fi
693	
694	    # Dependency security audit — target-declared manager, fail closed at moderate+.
695	    run_dependency_security_audit || exit 1
696	
697	    # Build and start
698	    log_info "Building Docker images..."
699	    # GIT_COMMIT was exported from the asserted SHA by materialize above — do NOT
700	    # re-resolve it from HEAD here (that would re-couple us to the shared checkout).
701	    # APP_VERSION is read from the SNAPSHOT so it matches the deployed commit.
702	    export APP_VERSION="$(node -p "require('$MAIA_BUILD_CONTEXT/package.json').version" 2>/dev/null || echo '1.0.0')"
703	    export BUILD_DATE="$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
704	    log_info "Deploying commit: $GIT_COMMIT (v$APP_VERSION)"
705	
706	    # Disk preflight — refuse BEFORE the storage-expanding build (a full-disk
707	    # build dies at metadata write after minutes and can exit 0 through ssh).
708	    "$SCRIPT_DIR/pre-deploy-gate.sh" disk
709	
710	    # Build image first (never rebuild while down!) — from the immutable snapshot
711	    # (compose reads MAIA_BUILD_CONTEXT for every build `context:`).
712	    # Build + swap use the SNAPSHOT's compose file (deploy_ctx_compose) — the
713	    # deployment structure is the authorized commit's (2026-09-03 provenance repair).
714	    deploy_ctx_compose build \
715	        --build-arg GIT_COMMIT="$GIT_COMMIT" \
716	        --build-arg APP_VERSION="$APP_VERSION" \
717	        --build-arg BUILD_DATE="$BUILD_DATE"
718	
719	    # PRE-swap: the built image must carry the asserted stamp; abort before any swap.
720	    deploy_ctx_verify_image "$GIT_COMMIT" "$MAIA_IMAGE_REPO:prod" || exit 1
721	
722	    # REVIEW-CUSTODY + DS-03: the exact pending relation must carry an
723	    # admitted review, exact old-reader compatibility, and failure-prefix safety.
724	    review_migration_custody_or_abort "Deployment"
725	
726	    # STEP 3: migrate while the reviewed old reader is still live. The helper
727	    # re-derives the pending set and re-witnesses the old reader immediately
728	    # before invoking the runner. Failure exits here, before tags or candidate swap.
729	    run_migrations_or_abort "Deployment"
730	
731	    # Only a successful pre-swap migration may advance rollback roles or the reader.
732	    tag_images_for_rollback "$GIT_COMMIT"
733	
734	    log_info "Starting containers after successful migrations..."
735	    deploy_ctx_compose up -d
736	
737	    log_info "Waiting for services to be healthy..."
738	    sleep 10
739	
740	    # Post-swap: assert the running container is the commit we authorized.
741	    if ! deploy_ctx_verify_running "$GIT_COMMIT"; then
742	        log_error "Post-swap provenance verification FAILED — the running container does not report the"
743	        log_error "authorized immutable commit $GIT_COMMIT. Migrations already succeeded pre-swap."
744	        log_error "The reviewed old reader was compatible with the resulting schema; restore the"
745	        log_error "previous reader image if the candidate cannot be made live:"
746	        log_error "  ./scripts/deploy-production.sh rollback"
747	        exit 1
748	    fi
749	
750	    log_success "Deployment complete!"
751	    echo ""
752	    cmd_status
753	
754	    # Run smoke tests and send alerts
755	    echo ""
756	    run_smoke_tests || log_warn "Some post-deploy checks failed"
757	}
758	
759	# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
760	# UPDATE - Pull latest and redeploy
761	# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
762	cmd_update() {
763	    # No commit is named yet — `update` names the tip it pulls, below. The
764	    # record is re-written with that SHA the moment the pull completes.
765	    acquire_deploy_lock "deploy-production.sh update" "pending (tip pulled by git pull; recorded once the pull completes)"
766	    log_info "Updating MAIA Sovereign..."
767	
768	    cd "$PROJECT_DIR"
769	
770	    log_info "Pulling latest code..."
771	    git pull
772	
773	    # Capture the pulled tip as an explicit, immutable SHA the instant the pull
774	    # completes, then build a SNAPSHOT of it. `update` legitimately means "build
775	    # the commit I just pulled" — but it must name that commit and freeze it, so
776	    # a concurrent checkout in the shared repo can't swap the build out from under
777	    # us. Sets MAIA_BUILD_CONTEXT + GIT_COMMIT.
778	    local pulled_sha
779	    pulled_sha="$(git -C "$PROJECT_DIR" rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null || true)"
780	    deploy_lock_record_target "$pulled_sha"
781	    deploy_ctx_assert_and_materialize "$pulled_sha" || exit 1
782	
783	    log_info "Rebuilding and redeploying..."
784	
785	    # Dependency security audit — target-declared manager, fail closed at moderate+.
786	    run_dependency_security_audit || exit 1
787	
788	    # GIT_COMMIT was exported from the pulled SHA by materialize above; APP_VERSION
789	    # is read from the SNAPSHOT so it matches the deployed commit.
790	    export APP_VERSION="$(node -p "require('$MAIA_BUILD_CONTEXT/package.json').version" 2>/dev/null || echo '1.0.0')"
791	    export BUILD_DATE="$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
792	    log_info "Deploying commit: $GIT_COMMIT (v$APP_VERSION)"
793	
794	    # Disk preflight — refuse BEFORE the storage-expanding build (a full-disk
795	    # build dies at metadata write after minutes and can exit 0 through ssh).
796	    "$SCRIPT_DIR/pre-deploy-gate.sh" disk
797	
798	    # Build + swap from the immutable snapshot — code AND compose structure
799	    # (deploy_ctx_compose; 2026-09-03 provenance repair).
800	    deploy_ctx_compose build \
801	        --build-arg GIT_COMMIT="$GIT_COMMIT" \
802	        --build-arg APP_VERSION="$APP_VERSION" \
803	        --build-arg BUILD_DATE="$BUILD_DATE"
804	
805	    # PRE-swap: the built image must carry the asserted stamp; abort before any swap.
806	    deploy_ctx_verify_image "$GIT_COMMIT" "$MAIA_IMAGE_REPO:prod" || exit 1
807	
808	    # REVIEW-CUSTODY + DS-03: same exact relation gate on update.
809	    review_migration_custody_or_abort "Update"
810	
811	    # STEP 3: no candidate reader is swapped until the reviewed schema transition
812	    # succeeds while the exact old reader remains live.
813	    run_migrations_or_abort "Update"
814	
815	    # Rollback roles advance only after the pre-swap schema transition succeeds.
816	    tag_images_for_rollback "$GIT_COMMIT"
817	
818	    deploy_ctx_compose up -d
819	
820	    # Post-swap: assert the running container is the commit we authorized.
821	    sleep 10
822	    if ! deploy_ctx_verify_running "$GIT_COMMIT"; then
823	        log_error "Post-swap provenance verification FAILED — the running container does not report the"
824	        log_error "authorized immutable commit $GIT_COMMIT. Migrations already succeeded pre-swap."
825	        log_error "The reviewed old reader was compatible with the resulting schema; restore the"
826	        log_error "previous reader image if the candidate cannot be made live:"
827	        log_error "  ./scripts/deploy-production.sh rollback"
828	        exit 1
829	    fi
830	
831	    log_success "Update complete!"
832	    cmd_status
833	
834	    # Run smoke tests and send alerts
835	    echo ""
836	    run_smoke_tests || log_warn "Some post-deploy checks failed"
837	}
838	
839	# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
840	# MIGRATE - Run database migrations only
841	# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
842	cmd_migrate() {
843	    acquire_deploy_lock "deploy-production.sh migrate" "migrations only (no image is built)"
844	    log_info "Running database migrations..."
845	
846	    cd "$PROJECT_DIR"
847	
848	    # Migration-only production acts are governed by the same bound review.
849	    review_migration_custody_or_abort "Migration-only run"
850	
851	    docker compose -f "$COMPOSE_FILE" --profile migrate run --rm migrate
852	
853	    log_success "Migrations complete!"
854	}
855	
856	# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
857	# LOGS - Tail container logs
858	# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
859	cmd_logs() {
860	    cd "$PROJECT_DIR"
861	    docker compose -f "$COMPOSE_FILE" logs -f --tail=100
862	}
863	
864	# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
865	# STATUS - Show container status
866	# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
867	cmd_status() {
868	    cd "$PROJECT_DIR"
869	    echo ""
870	    log_info "Container Status:"
871	    docker compose -f "$COMPOSE_FILE" ps
872	    echo ""
873	    log_info "Health Check:"
874	    docker compose -f "$COMPOSE_FILE" ps --format "table {{.Name}}\t{{.Status}}"
875	}
876	
877	# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
878	# STOP - Stop all containers
879	# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
880	cmd_stop() {
881	    log_info "Stopping MAIA Sovereign..."
882	
883	    cd "$PROJECT_DIR"
884	    docker compose -f "$COMPOSE_FILE" down
885	
886	    log_success "All containers stopped."
887	}
888	
889	# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
890	# BACKUP - Backup PostgreSQL database
891	# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
892	cmd_backup() {
893	    BACKUP_FILE="$PROJECT_DIR/backups/maia_backup_$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S).sql"
894	
895	    log_info "Backing up database to $BACKUP_FILE..."
896	
897	    mkdir -p "$PROJECT_DIR/backups"
898	
899	    docker compose -f "$COMPOSE_FILE" exec -T postgres \
900	        pg_dump -U soullab maia_consciousness > "$BACKUP_FILE"
901	
902	    log_success "Backup saved to: $BACKUP_FILE"
903	}
904	
905	# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
906	# RESTORE - Restore PostgreSQL database
907	# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
908	cmd_restore() {
909	    if [ -z "$1" ]; then
910	        log_error "Usage: ./deploy-production.sh restore <backup_file.sql>"
911	        exit 1
912	    fi
913	
914	    BACKUP_FILE="$1"
915	
916	    if [ ! -f "$BACKUP_FILE" ]; then
917	        log_error "Backup file not found: $BACKUP_FILE"
918	        exit 1
919	    fi
920	
921	    log_warn "This will REPLACE all data in the database!"
922	    read -p "Are you sure? (yes/no): " confirm
923	
924	    if [ "$confirm" != "yes" ]; then
925	        log_info "Restore cancelled."
926	        exit 0
927	    fi
928	
929	    log_info "Restoring database from $BACKUP_FILE..."
930	
931	    docker compose -f "$COMPOSE_FILE" exec -T postgres \
932	        psql -U soullab maia_consciousness < "$BACKUP_FILE"
933	
934	    log_success "Database restored!"
935	}
936	
937	# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
938	# SMOKE - Run smoke tests manually
939	# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
940	cmd_smoke() {
941	    log_info "Running smoke tests against production..."
942	    cd "$PROJECT_DIR"
943	    run_smoke_tests
944	}
945	
946	# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
947	# ROLLBACK - Instant rollback to previous deployment
948	# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
949	# Two-command rollback: swap image tags, restart container
950	# No rebuild required - just swap and go
951	cmd_rollback() {
952	    acquire_deploy_lock "deploy-production.sh rollback" "maia-sovereign:previous (image tag swap; no commit is built)"
953	    log_info "Rolling back to previous deployment..."
954	
955	    cd "$PROJECT_DIR"
956	
957	    # Check if previous image exists
958	    if ! docker image inspect maia-sovereign:previous >/dev/null 2>&1; then
959	        log_error "No previous image found. Cannot rollback."
960	        log_info "Previous images are created during deploy. Run deploy at least twice."
961	        exit 1
962	    fi
963	
964	    # Get current and previous commit SHAs from labels
965	    CURRENT_SHA=$(docker inspect --format='{{index .Config.Labels "git.commit"}}' maia-sovereign:current 2>/dev/null || echo "unknown")
966	    PREVIOUS_SHA=$(docker inspect --format='{{index .Config.Labels "git.commit"}}' maia-sovereign:previous 2>/dev/null || echo "unknown")
967	
968	    log_info "Current deployment: $CURRENT_SHA"
969	    log_info "Rolling back to: $PREVIOUS_SHA"
970	
971	    # Resolve image identities before moving any role tags.
972	    local current_id previous_id
973	    current_id="$(docker image inspect maia-sovereign:current --format '{{.Id}}')"
974	    previous_id="$(docker image inspect maia-sovereign:previous --format '{{.Id}}')"
975	    if [ -z "$current_id" ] || [ -z "$previous_id" ]; then
976	        log_error "Rollback image identity is incomplete; refusing to move role tags."
977	        exit 1
978	    fi
979	
980	    # Compose launches maia-sovereign:prod, not :current. Therefore rollback must
981	    # move the previous image onto BOTH role tags before recreating the reader.
982	    log_info "Swapping image tags..."
983	    docker tag maia-sovereign:current maia-sovereign:broken
984	    docker tag maia-sovereign:previous maia-sovereign:current
985	    docker tag maia-sovereign:previous maia-sovereign:prod
986	
987	    # Restart only the application reader. A reader rollback must not restart
988	    # Postgres or any other dependency.
989	    log_info "Restarting MAIA with previous image..."
990	    docker compose -f "$COMPOSE_FILE" up -d --force-recreate --no-deps maia
991	
992	    # Wait for health
993	    log_info "Waiting for service to be healthy..."
994	    sleep 10
995	
996	    # Verify both health and that Compose actually launched the previous image.
997	    local running_id running_git
998	    running_id="$(docker inspect maia-sovereign --format '{{.Image}}' 2>/dev/null || true)"
999	    running_git="$(docker exec maia-sovereign printenv GIT_COMMIT 2>/dev/null || true)"
1000	    if docker compose -f "$COMPOSE_FILE" ps | grep -q "healthy" \
1001	       && [ "$running_id" = "$previous_id" ]; then
1002	        log_success "Rollback complete! Now running: ${running_git:-$PREVIOUS_SHA}"
1003	
1004	        # Move the former reader to :previous so an explicit roll-forward remains possible.
1005	        docker tag maia-sovereign:broken maia-sovereign:previous
1006	
1007	        send_alert "warning" "Rollback executed" "{\"from\": \"$CURRENT_SHA\", \"to\": \"${running_git:-$PREVIOUS_SHA}\"}"
1008	    else
1009	        log_error "Rollback verification FAILED."
1010	        log_error "Expected running image: $previous_id"
1011	        log_error "Observed running image: ${running_id:-<missing>}"
1012	        cmd_status
1013	        exit 1
1014	    fi
1015	}
1016	
1017	# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
1018	# SAFE-MODE - Toggle safe mode for degraded operation
1019	# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
1020	# When something weird happens in prod, flip one switch and the app stays usable
1021	cmd_safe_mode() {
1022	    local mode="${1:-status}"
1023	    cd "$PROJECT_DIR"
1024	
1025	    case "$mode" in
1026	        on|enable|1)
1027	            log_info "Enabling safe mode..."
1028	
1029	            # Set SAFE_MODE=1 in .env.production if not already set
1030	            if grep -q "^SAFE_MODE=" .env.production 2>/dev/null; then
1031	                if [[ "$OSTYPE" == "darwin"* ]]; then
1032	                    sed -i '' 's/^SAFE_MODE=.*/SAFE_MODE=1/' .env.production
1033	                else
1034	                    sed -i 's/^SAFE_MODE=.*/SAFE_MODE=1/' .env.production
1035	                fi
1036	            else
1037	                echo "SAFE_MODE=1" >> .env.production
1038	            fi
1039	
1040	            # Restart maia to pick up the change
1041	            log_info "Restarting MAIA in safe mode..."
1042	            docker compose -f "$COMPOSE_FILE" up -d maia
1043	
1044	            log_success "Safe mode ENABLED. Non-essential features disabled."
1045	            log_warn "Disabled features: geocode, astrology, heavy memory, exports, advanced voice"
1046	            send_alert "warning" "Safe mode enabled" "{\"reason\": \"manual toggle\"}"
1047	            ;;
1048	
1049	        off|disable|0)
1050	            log_info "Disabling safe mode..."
1051	
1052	            # Set SAFE_MODE=0 in .env.production
1053	            if grep -q "^SAFE_MODE=" .env.production 2>/dev/null; then
1054	                if [[ "$OSTYPE" == "darwin"* ]]; then
1055	                    sed -i '' 's/^SAFE_MODE=.*/SAFE_MODE=0/' .env.production
1056	                else
1057	                    sed -i 's/^SAFE_MODE=.*/SAFE_MODE=0/' .env.production
1058	                fi
1059	            else
1060	                echo "SAFE_MODE=0" >> .env.production
1061	            fi
1062	
1063	            # Restart maia to pick up the change
1064	            log_info "Restarting MAIA with full features..."
1065	            docker compose -f "$COMPOSE_FILE" up -d maia
1066	
1067	            log_success "Safe mode DISABLED. All features enabled."
1068	            send_alert "info" "Safe mode disabled" "{\"reason\": \"manual toggle\"}"
1069	            ;;
1070	
1071	        status|*)
1072	            # Check current status
1073	            local current
1074	            current=$(grep "^SAFE_MODE=" .env.production 2>/dev/null | cut -d'=' -f2 || echo "0")
1075	
1076	            if [ "$current" = "1" ] || [ "$current" = "true" ]; then
1077	                log_warn "Safe mode is currently ENABLED"
1078	                echo "  Disabled features: geocode, astrology, heavy memory, exports, advanced voice"
1079	                echo "  To disable: ./scripts/deploy-production.sh safe-mode off"
1080	            else
1081	                log_info "Safe mode is currently DISABLED (all features enabled)"
1082	                echo "  To enable: ./scripts/deploy-production.sh safe-mode on"
1083	            fi
1084	            ;;
1085	    esac
1086	}
1087	
1088	# tag_images_for_rollback moved to scripts/deploy-tag.sh (sourced above) so the
1089	# quick pre-deploy-gate.sh deploy-maia path refreshes rollback tags too.
1090	
1091	# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
1092	# MAIN
1093	# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
1094	case "${1:-help}" in
1095	    setup)
1096	        cmd_setup
1097	        ;;
1098	    deploy)
1099	        cmd_deploy "$2"
1100	        ;;
1101	    update)
1102	        cmd_update
1103	        ;;
1104	    migrate)
1105	        cmd_migrate
1106	        ;;
1107	    logs)
1108	        cmd_logs
1109	        ;;
1110	    status)
1111	        cmd_status
1112	        ;;
1113	    stop)
1114	        cmd_stop
1115	        ;;
1116	    backup)
1117	        cmd_backup
1118	        ;;
1119	    restore)
1120	        cmd_restore "$2"
1121	        ;;
1122	    smoke)
1123	        cmd_smoke
1124	        ;;
1125	    smoke-prod)
1126	        log_info "Running smoke tests against production (soullab.life)..."
1127	        BASE_URL="https://soullab.life" run_smoke_tests
1128	        ;;
1129	    rollback)
1130	        cmd_rollback
1131	        ;;
1132	    safe-mode)
1133	        cmd_safe_mode "$2"
1134	        ;;
1135	    *)
1136	        echo "MAIA Sovereign - Production Deployment"
1137	        echo ""
1138	        echo "Usage: $0 <command>"
1139	        echo ""
1140	        echo "Commands:"
1141	        echo "  setup       - First-time setup (generate secrets)"
1142	        echo "  deploy <SHA> - Build+deploy the full stack from a NAMED immutable commit"
1143	        echo "                 (no SHA + DEPLOY_ALLOW_HEAD=1 → build current checkout tip, ack)"
1144	        echo "  update      - Pull latest code, then build the pulled tip as an immutable snapshot"
1145	        echo "  rollback   - Instant rollback to previous deployment"
1146	        echo "  safe-mode  - Toggle safe mode (on/off/status)"
1147	        echo "  migrate    - Run database migrations"
1148	        echo "  logs       - Tail container logs"
1149	        echo "  status     - Show container status"
1150	        echo "  stop       - Stop all containers"
1151	        echo "  backup     - Backup database"
1152	        echo "  restore    - Restore database from backup"
1153	        echo "  smoke      - Run smoke tests (uses BASE_URL from .env.production)"
1154	        echo "  smoke-prod - Run smoke tests against soullab.life (always)"
1155	        echo ""
1156	        echo "Stability:"
1157	        echo "  rollback   - Swap back to previous image (no rebuild)"
1158	        echo "  safe-mode on  - Disable non-essential features"
1159	        echo "  safe-mode off - Re-enable all features"
